question: A roulette wheel has 38 numbers; a winning $1 bet pays $35 plus your stake. You bet $1 on every number. What happens each spin?
answer: You lose $2 a spin: $38 staked, $36 back. Covering every number turns a bad bet into a certain loss. If a win paid $39, the same cover would gain $2 a spin: the casino’s position. Graham’s point: diversifying works only on top of a margin of safety, an edge in your favour.
move: Before spreading your bets, check that each one is worth making.
trap: ‘You break even’: one number always wins, so every bet seems covered.
simply: Buying every ticket in a raffle means you will win the prize, but if all the tickets cost more than the prize, you lose money every single time.
why: It is the test for any spread-out plan, from a portfolio of shares to a stack of side projects: owning many things only smooths the results; it cannot turn poor odds into good ones. Each piece has to be worth having on its own.
